chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Al-Hasan ibn Salih, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who was found killed, so two men came to his guardian. One of them said, 'I killed him deliberately,' and the other said, 'I killed him in error.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'If he accepts the word of the one who killed deliberately, then there is no way for him against the one who killed in error; and if he accepts the word of the one who killed in error, then there is no way for him against the one who killed deliberately.'

key_terms.سَبِيلٌ: Way / Means / Path (here: legal claim or liability)

ai.seo_question: How is blood money distributed when two people claim to have killed the same person, one deliberately and one accidentally?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the principle of 'ikhtiyar' (choice) for the wali al-dam, allowing him to select either the deliberate or accidental killer for full liability, thereby exempting the other. This ruling highlights the flexibility in Shia jurisprudence regarding conflicting testimonies in homicide cases, prioritizing the guardian's discretion over simultaneous dual liability. It reflects the broader legal maxim that when claims are mutually exclusive yet individually valid, the authority may choose one to resolve the dispute definitively.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, form Al Hassan Bin Mahboub, from Al Hassan Bin Salih who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about a man who was found killed, so two men came over to his guardian, so one of the two said, ‘I killed him deliberately’, and the other one said, ‘I killed him in error’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If he takes to the words of the one with the deliberation, so there is no way for him upon the one with the error; and if he were to take to the words of the one with the error, so there is no way for him against the one with the deliberation’.
